test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some roses are pink.

All pink are pigs.

Some pigs are birds.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some birds are pink.

II. Some pigs are pink.

III. Some pigs are roses.

IV. Some birds are roses.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6c4020325568bf30885a0db1aad0ed24119d4b1fe34e972ea9fea2af06af527.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some birds are pink → **Does not** follow (As some pigs are birds and all pink are pigs. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some pigs are pink → Follow (As all pink are pigs. As whole pinks comes in pigs, therefore it is true.)

III. Some pigs are roses → Follow (As some roses are pink and all pink are pigs. As whole pinks comes in pigs and has some part common with roses, therefore it is true.)

IV. Some birds are roses → Does not follow (As some roses are pink, all pink are pigs and some pigs are birds. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only II and III follow.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
